opening.text: In a good choir, no one sings the same note. Some voices are high, some are low. Some are soft, some are strong. But they listen to each other, and they follow the same song. The result is something no single voice could make. That is what unity sounds like.

mainMessage.text: Unity is many different voices singing one song, and Jesus Christ is the song.

blocks.text: **One song** A choir needs a song to follow. For us, it is Jesus Christ.
That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “One in Christ” from the April 2023 general conference.
Only in Jesus Christ can we truly become one.
He is the song.
**Different voices, one choir** A choir with one voice isn't a choir. We don't have to sound alike.
For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “One in Christ” from the April 2023 general conference.
Unity does not require sameness, but it does require harmony.
Harmony, not sameness.
**The loud voice** One singer who wants to be heard above all the rest spoils the sound.
Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Our Hearts Knit as One” from the October 2008 general conference.
Pride is the great enemy of unity.
Put pride down.
**More in common** The singers in a choir may come from different places. But they sing the same words.
For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office: So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Our Hearts Knit as One” from the October 2008 general conference.
The children of God have more in common than they have differences.
We share the same song.
**Hearts knit together** Heavenly Father wants us close, the way a choir leans in to hear each other.

And he commanded them that there should be no contention one with another, but that they should look forward with one eye, having one faith and one baptism, having their hearts knit together in unity and in love one towards another.
Elder Henry B. Eyring of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “That We May Be One” from the April 1998 general conference.
Our Heavenly Father wants our hearts to be knit together.
Lean in and listen.
**The joy of the song** Singing together is a joy. Unity brings the same joy to a people.

And it came to pass that there was no contention in the land, because of the love of God which did dwell in the hearts of the people. And there were no envyings, nor strifes, nor tumults, nor whoredoms, nor lyings, nor murders, nor any manner of lasciviousness; and surely there could not be a happier people among all the people who had been created by the hand of God.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Our Hearts Knit as One” from the October 2008 general conference.
We can pray and work for the unity that will bring us joy and multiply our power to serve.

story.title: Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands

blocks.text: Israel was fighting a battle. As long as Moses held up his hand, they prevailed.

And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
Moses couldn't hold on alone. Two friends stood on either side and held his arms. Unity is holding each other up when one of us is tired.

story.title: Nehemiah rebuilds the wall

blocks.text: Jerusalem's wall lay in ruins. The people had enemies and little time.
So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.
Everyone took a piece. The wall rose together. They did it because they were willing to work as one.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt they truly belonged to a group. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The people of Alma

blocks.text: In the church under Alma, priest and people worked side by side. No one felt above another.

And when the priests left their labor to impart the word of God unto the people, the people also left their labors to hear the word of God. And when the priest had imparted unto them the word of God they all returned again diligently unto their labors; and the priest, not esteeming himself above his hearers, for the preacher was no better than the hearer, neither was the teacher any better than the learner; and thus they were all equal, and they did all labor, every man according to his strength.
Everyone worked. No one stood above the rest. That is how unity is built: as equals who share the work.
